subject: Genetics
title: Designing the Guide RNA
description: A 60-second lesson on Designing the Guide RNA.

hook.text: You want to edit a gene. Step one: design a 20-letter RNA sequence that matches your target.

buildup.text: The guide must match only one spot in 3 billion letters. Off-target matches mean unintended cuts elsewhere.

discovery.text: Algorithms score potential guides by uniqueness. The best guides match one location perfectly and nothing else.

twist.text: The target site needs a PAM sequence—a short code next to the cut site. No PAM, no cut. It limits where you can edit.

climax.text: New Cas variants recognize different PAMs, expanding the editable genome. Engineers are removing nature's restrictions.

punchline.text: Twenty letters. One target. Billions of possibilities.

quiz.question: What is a PAM sequence?
options: A required code next to the CRISPR cut site
